title: Choose the ShipBrief composition
question: All three screens combine the 3D streaming push wall with the layered reference-manual evidence. Choose the information layout that feels clearest.

options.label: Wall + open evidence layers
options.lineage: Horizontal push wall with a split evidence-and-draft workspace
options.thesis: Scan the push wall, then inspect commits on clear layers beside the draft.
options.viewport: A focused tile lifts from a horizontal row; the selected push opens commit, file, and compare leaves beside a readable draft sheet.
options.risk: Three simultaneous regions may feel dense; the selected tile and draft stay dominant.

options.label: Vertical push rail + source leaves
options.lineage: A vertical push stack with a central selected record and fanned acetate sources
options.thesis: Keep the queue in reach while linked source layers fan open next to the selected push.
options.viewport: A vertical stack keeps incoming pushes visible; the selected push occupies the center and its sources fan open to the right above review controls.
options.risk: The vertical queue consumes width on smaller screens and will need a compact rail state.

options.label: Draft-first reading sheet
options.lineage: An editorial draft sheet with a horizontal push rail and stepped source tabs
options.thesis: Give the draft room to read, with pushes and commit sources immediately nearby.
options.viewport: A narrow push row sits above a large draft sheet; acetate source tabs open along the right margin and review actions stay fixed below.
options.risk: The large draft canvas makes the evidence rail less prominent until a source tab opens.
